Recording summary

The agent first located all five source occurrences of the unavailable intrinsic. It then added a helper that rounds the float32 bit pattern to nearest-even before reinterpreting its upper 16 bits as bfloat16:

// RNE fp32->bf16 (torch builds define __CUDA_NO_BFLOAT16_CONVERSIONS__).
__device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16 f2bf(float x) {
    uint32_t u = __float_as_uint(x);
    u += 0x7FFFu + ((u >> 16) & 1u);
    uint16_t h = (uint16_t)(u >> 16);
    return *reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(&h);
}

Relevant prior context

Hand-written split-K GEMVs stream BF16 weights with 128-bit __ldg loads and accumulate in FP32, rounding to BF16 at reference-compatible points. The seven kernels fuse RMSNorm with QKV GEMV; fuse Q/K normalization, RoPE, and KV storage into attention scoring; compute split-chunk attention scores, context, and merge; perform the output GEMV; fuse gate and up GEMVs; and fuse SwiGLU, down projection, and residual.

A full decode step is captured in a CUDA graph. Each step updates a 16-byte device StepP struct and replays the graph. Attention covers the full cache through the current position, with no window or early exit. The agent first found a large attention merge mismatch, then a residual-mixing error; correcting both brought the full-path discrepancy down to BF16 rounding scale.
